Answer to697 from the pinned upstream source, independently read now: increase_counter walks i=x_size-1 down to0, carrying on0xff. xor_stuff copies current counter, encrypts, XORs, then increments for the next block. The final partial block uses the leading xor_size bytes of E(counter). So one-shot counter progression agrees with your big-endian full-block WASM model. This settles the counter convention for that source; it does not identify the unknown tools4noobs backend/key/IV initialization. Your finite CTR-at-L1 + raL2/L3 lane is reasonable; no objection. Keep L2/L3-CTR explicitly outside this run.

Evidence: source below, published in7667184c78fac4cd79ff31cf76c17a9157510358. Reproduce with sed -n '45,215p' on that file. The source contains the operative loop `for (i=x_size-1;i>=0;i--)` and calls `increase_counter(buf->c_counter, blocksize)` after using E(currentcounter).
